items.content_html:
FF142 adds support for the dictionary property RTCRtpEncodingParameters.codec in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1894137

This is used when setting encodings in RTCRtpSender.setParameters(parameter.encodings) and RTCPeerConnection.addTransceiver(sendencodings), and returned in RTCRtpSender/getParameters() (encodings.codec).

This updates the set/getParameters on the sender. The transceiver just references the sender, so doesn't need an update.

Related docs work can be tracked in #40477
items.title: RTCRtpSender.get/setParameters - encodings.codec property

items.content_html:
Description

Clarify that backdrop-filter only affects the backdrop image up to its nearest ancestor Backdrop Root as stated in the issue, and add a concise note listing what triggers a Backdrop Root which was obtained from the source listed in this PR.

Motivation

The existing text (“area behind an element”) implied that backdrop-filter applies to all pixels behind an element, which contradicts real-world behavior and the Filter Effects Level 2 specification. Developers encountered “missing” blur outside the nearest Backdrop Root (for example, a semi-transparent ancestor), leading to confusion. This update aligns MDN’s description with the spec and addresses user reports in the GitHub issue.

Additional details

  • Filter Effects Level 2 (Backdrop Root definition)
    https://drafts.fxtf.org/filter-effects-2/#BackdropRoot
  • Live demo showing blur limited to the nearest Backdrop Root
    https://jsfiddle.net/xer31ywj/

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #40602
items.title: fix issue: Backdrop Root concept undocumented

items.content_html: After #40228, we are a lot more explicit on some CSS stylistic decisions. In particular, we now have systematic rules surrounding the preferred color notations. As a starter, I'm porting all colors that have named equivalents to named colors, per our recommendation of using "common named colors". Afterwards, I'm going to convert the remaining colors to the preferred notation, such as preferring rgb() and preferring number parameters.
items.title: Lint: use named color if possible (6)

items.content_html:
FF142 Animation/commitStyles() allows animations to capture the final styles without specifying a fill in latest spec.

Note that normally I'd have the new behavior front and center and mention the older behavior as a legacy thing. Unfortunately the advice of the developer is that you can't feature check for this, so people will have to stick with the old behaviour until this is in most browsers.
So this update covers the old case first, and puts the new information second.

Related docs work in #40482
items.title: FF142 Animation.commitStyles() automatically fills values

items.content_html:
Description

Corrects the Safari origin and overall storage quota values to match WebKit’s official policy and clarifies the distinction between browser apps, web apps, and non-browser WebViews, just as requested in the issue.

Motivation

As stated in the issue, the current numbers in the MDN documentation for Safari’s per-origin quota (20% vs 60%) and overall quota (15% vs 80%) were inverted and the role of WebViews versus standalone web apps was unclear. Updating these values ensures MDN reflects the current WebKit storage policy and prevents developers from planning around incorrect limits.

Additional details

The issue referenced pull request #28510, which uses the Webkit article and has the numbers flipped.
WebKit article: https://www.webkit.org/blog/14403/updates-to-storage-policy/

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #40394
items.title: Modify Safari storage quota based on WebKit resource
